bibl.title: Neural Networks of the Mouse Neocortex

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how areas across the entire mouse neocortex organise into communication networks, mapped by over 600 traced pathways
span.quote: Numerous studies have examined the neuronal inputs and/or outputs of many areas of the brain cortex, but how these areas organize into broader communication networks across the cortex is unclear.

span.label: how do different cortical areas communicate at the network level across the whole structure
span.quote: For the cerebral cortex, a brain structure involved in regulating cognition, motivation, and emotion, it remains largely unclear how different areas across the entire structure communicate at the network level to guide its complex functions.

span.label: delivers a cortical connectivity atlas and matrices from uniformly collected tracer data, and finds the neocortex clusters into four somatic sensorimotor, two medial and two lateral subnetworks
span.quote: The connectivity matrices and cortical map revealed that the entire cortex is organized into four somatic sensorimotor, two medial, and two lateral subnetworks that display unique topologies and can interact through select cortical areas.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The connectivity matrices and cortical map revealed that the entire cortex is organized into four somatic sensorimotor, two medial, and two lateral subnetworks that display unique topologies and can interact through select cortical areas.

span.label: cortico-cortical connectivity of the mouse neocortex
span.quote: For the cerebral cortex, a brain structure involved in regulating cognition, motivation, and emotion, it remains largely unclear how different areas across the entire structure communicate at the network level to guide its complex functions.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We generated a cortical connectivity atlas, which accommodates over 600 labeled neural pathways from tracer injections applied across the entire neocortex.

span.label: each injection is designed to return four kinds of information at once - inputs, outputs, reciprocal connections and intermediate stations - by pairing an anterograde with a retrograde tracer
span.quote: The MCP neuronal connectivity data was produced using double co-injection tract tracing ( Thompson and Swanson, 2010 ), which simultaneously reveals four types of information for a given region (i.e. A): its (1) inputs (A←B), (2) outputs (A→B), (3) reciprocal or recurrent connections (A⇔B), and (4) intermediate stations, which bridge brain structures that are not directly connected

span.label: the two tracer directions are used as independent measurements of the same connection, and their agreement is reported as a validity check
span.quote: Iterating through each matrix entry, 89% of connections exhibited mutual labeling by both anterograde and retrograde labeling methods, suggesting that the datasets were significantly similar.

span.label: injection specificity is cross-validated by tracing the reverse direction: retrograde tracer into the regions the anterograde labelling had targeted
span.quote: The specificity of injections are cross-validated by the application of retrograde tracers to regions targeted by anterogradely labeled axon terminals and vice versa ( Figure S1 for details on data validation).

span.label: the subnetworks are not stipulated but produced by reordering the matrix with a clustering algorithm, and named afterwards
span.quote: To reveal subnetworks, a composite matrix was constructed in which the nodes (ROIs) were reordered via a clustering algorithm ( Figure 2E ; Supplemental Materials for annotation and analysis details).

span.label: the clustering makes the matrix diagonal readable as within-subnetwork density and the off-diagonal as between-subnetwork traffic
span.quote: The clustering orders nodes into modules that maximize the connectivity and arrange highly interconnected nodes such that they are clustered along the matrix diagonal, facilitating visualization of grouped regions that can be considered subnetworks.

span.label: the whole analysis rests on hand annotation, because no tool can identify fine anatomic boundaries, and the strengths recorded are semi-quantitative
span.quote: Currently, informatics tools that automatically and precisely identify fine anatomic boundaries in histological brain sections are non-existent. Consequently, analysis of the data necessitates manual annotation to index anatomic locations and semi-quantitative strengths of labeled cortico-cortical pathways.

span.label: each pathway is rendered as a separate layer in a common anatomic frame so that arbitrary combinations can be viewed together
span.quote: The second method consists of manually rendering the observed labeling patterns using Adobe Photoshop. Each pathway is rendered in a separate layer and all layers across all experiments are stacked to allow for a composite view of labeling trends.

span.label: uniform collection and analysis is claimed as the advantage over connectivity matrices assembled from published literature
span.quote: In contrast, the networks reported here are based on data collected and analyzed in a homogenous fashion rather than gathered piecemeal from the literature.

span.label: the somatosensory subdivisions used as network nodes are themselves validated against known somatotopy in the brainstem before being used
span.quote: 240 intracortical connections were manually reconstructed within a common neuroanatomic framework, forming a cortico-cortical connectivity map that facilitates comparison of connections from different cortical targets.

span.label: a visualisation artefact is disclosed rather than left for the reader to discover: the injection sites look larger than they are once the image is brightened enough to show fine fibers
span.quote: The size of co-injections are ~ 250-500μm and mostly confined within individual cortical areas ( Figure 1B ), although when images are adjusted to reveal fine fibers, injection sites are overexposed, misrepresenting their actual size ( Figure S1A ).

span.label: the resource is framed as the input to later causal work, naming the specific techniques that would test any mapped pathway
span.quote: Moreover, these projections may be assessed functionally using available optogenetic techniques that allow one to measure the circuit-level or behavioral consequences of manipulating a given pathway within a neural network ( Yizhar et al., 2011 ).

span.label: Interpreting large-scale connectivity data remains an unsolved challenge.
span.note: what this limits: the interpretive claims, not the resource: the paper demonstrates THE FEASIBILITY OF PRODUCING AND COLLECTING LARGE-SCALE CONNECTIVITY DATA, and names interpretation as the unsolved part
span.quote: In conclusion, we and other groups have demonstrated the feasibility of producing and collecting large-scale connectivity data ( Osten and Margrie, 2013 ; Pollock et al., 2014 ); however, interpretation of this wealth of anatomical data presents an ongoing challenge.

span.label: Published injection-site images overstate the true injection size.
span.note: what this limits: any reading of injection extent from the published figures: WHEN IMAGES ARE ADJUSTED TO REVEAL FINE FIBERS, INJECTION [extent appears larger] than the ~250-500um stated
span.quote: The size of co-injections are ~ 250-500μm and mostly confined within individual cortical areas ( Figure 1B ), although when images are adjusted to reveal fine fibers, injection sites are overexposed, misrepresenting their actual size ( Figure S1A ).

span.label: Annotation had to be done by hand because no automated tool can delineate fine anatomical boundaries.
span.note: what this limits: the precision of every areal boundary in the atlas: INFORMATICS TOOLS THAT AUTOMATICALLY AND PRECISELY IDENTIFY FINE ANATOMIC BOUNDARIES ... ARE NON-EXISTENT, so annotation is by hand
span.quote: Currently, informatics tools that automatically and precisely identify fine anatomic boundaries in histological brain sections are non-existent.

span.label: The mapped long-range interactions have not been validated at the synaptic or cell-type level.
span.note: what this limits: the synaptic and cell-type reading of any mapped connection: these MAY BE VALIDATED AT THE SYNAPTIC LEVEL USING TRANSSYNAPTIC VIRAL TRACING - not done here
span.quote: Any of these long range interactions may be validated at the synaptic level using transsynaptic viral tracing and may be further investigated to determine cell-type specific connections using methods such as channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping ( Luo et al., 2008 ; Osakada et al., 2011 ; Petreanu et al., 2009 ).

span.label: interpreting connectivity data at this scale is named as the unsolved part, not the collection of it
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - collection is demonstrated, interpretation is not
span.quote: In conclusion, we and other groups have demonstrated the feasibility of producing and collecting large-scale connectivity data ( Osten and Margrie, 2013 ; Pollock et al., 2014 ); however, interpretation of this wealth of anatomical data presents an ongoing challenge.

span.label: no automated tool exists for the annotation step, so the atlas is hand-made and semi-quantitative
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2, with the consequence: the analysis is hand-made and semi-quantitative
span.quote: Currently, informatics tools that automatically and precisely identify fine anatomic boundaries in histological brain sections are non-existent. Consequently, analysis of the data necessitates manual annotation to index anatomic locations and semi-quantitative strengths of labeled cortico-cortical pathways.

span.label: the matrices discard route, laminar specificity and topography, which the authors call critical features of networks
span.note: what this limits: every use of the connectivity matrices: THEY EXCLUDE DETAILS LIKE PROJECTIONS ROUTES, LAMINAR SPECIFICITY OF PROJECTIONS, OR TOPOGRAPHICAL organisation - the condensed view drops features the authors call critical
span.quote: The matrices provide a condensed view of cortical connectivity patterns, but exclude details like projections routes, laminar specificity of projections, or topographical and topological connectivity patterns, which are critical features of networks.

span.label: the mapped connections are anatomical and require separate validation at the synaptic and functional level
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 3 - anatomical connections, awaiting synaptic and functional validation
span.quote: Any of these long range interactions may be validated at the synaptic level using transsynaptic viral tracing and may be further investigated to determine cell-type specific connections using methods such as channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping ( Luo et al., 2008 ; Osakada et al., 2011 ; Petreanu et al., 2009 ).

span.label: human network findings are held to need validation in animal models at higher resolution, which is the gap this atlas is built to fill
span.note: what this limits: the transfer of human network findings: IT IS NECESSARY TO VALIDATE THESE NETWORKS USING RELIABLE NEURAL TRACT TRACING METHODS IN ANIMAL MODELS AT A HIGHER RESOLUTION
span.quote: Nevertheless, it is necessary to validate these networks using reliable neural tract tracing methods in animal models at a higher resolution, which will facilitate exploration of the molecular and cellular etiologies of these disorders.

span.label: the hub - a region of high network interaction - imported to interpret the claustrum and lateral entorhinal area
span.quote: The insular and temporal areas along the lateral aspect of the cortex formed two distinct clusters and the broad and unique intracortical connections of the claustrum and lateral entorhinal area suggest they may serve as hubs, or regions of high network interaction ( Sporns, 2010 ).

span.label: reordering nodes so that dense groups fall along the diagonal, which converts a connectivity table into a set of named subnetworks
span.quote: The clustering orders nodes into modules that maximize the connectivity and arrange highly interconnected nodes such that they are clustered along the matrix diagonal, facilitating visualization of grouped regions that can be considered subnetworks.

span.label: cross-validating anterograde injection specificity by applying retrograde tracers to the regions targeted by anterogradely labelled axon terminals, and the reverse
span.note: eliminates: that the anterograde labelling reflects nonspecific injection spread rather than a genuine projection · outcome: held
span.quote: The specificity of injections are cross-validated by the application of retrograde tracers to regions targeted by anterogradely labeled axon terminals and vice versa ( Figure S1 for details on data validation).

span.label: connectome - as the C. elegans-style complete synaptic wiring diagram versus as the meso-scale regional map this paper builds
span.quote: Unlike the recently assembled connectome of the C. elegans ( White et al., 1986 ; Jarrell et al., 2012 ), wiring diagrams for mammalian species have been assembled on substantially smaller scales and for specific functional systems ( Felleman and Van Essen, 1991 ; Saleem et al., 2008 ).

span.label: cortical network - as derived from human fMRI and diffusion imaging versus as traced anatomically in an animal model; the paper treats the second as validation of the first
span.quote: Nevertheless, it is necessary to validate these networks using reliable neural tract tracing methods in animal models at a higher resolution, which will facilitate exploration of the molecular and cellular etiologies of these disorders.

span.label: connectivity matrix - assembled piecemeal from published literature versus collected and analysed uniformly; the paper claims the difference matters
span.quote: In contrast, the networks reported here are based on data collected and analyzed in a homogenous fashion rather than gathered piecemeal from the literature.

span.label: subnetwork - as a cluster in a reordered matrix versus as an anatomically or functionally defined system; here the first produces the second, and the names come last
span.quote: The clustering orders nodes into modules that maximize the connectivity and arrange highly interconnected nodes such that they are clustered along the matrix diagonal, facilitating visualization of grouped regions that can be considered subnetworks.

span.label: primary sensory cortex as strictly unisensory versus as cross-modally modulated - a boundary the connectivity data is said to challenge
span.quote: This supports the concept of cross-modal modulation, which challenges the idea that mammalian primary sensory cortices are strictly unisensory

span.label: connection strength - as a semi-quantitative hand-graded density, which is what the weights in every matrix here actually are
span.quote: The first is for the purpose of constructing a comprehensive connectivity database and is comprised of an excel sheet that indexes anatomic locations and corresponding semi-quantitative densities of labeling (PHAL labeled axons/terminal boutons; CTb and FG labeled neurons).

span.label: claim_type: method
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: existence — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Together, these data provide a resource that can be used to further investigate cortical networks and their corresponding functions.

span.label: method: double co-injection tract tracing, one anterograde and one retrograde tracer per site, across the whole neocortex, hand-annotated into weighted directional matrices and clustered
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: system-or-tool-building — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: The MCP neuronal connectivity data was produced using double co-injection tract tracing ( Thompson and Swanson, 2010 ), which simultaneously reveals four types of information for a given region (i.e. A): its (1) inputs (A←B), (2) outputs (A→B), (3) reciprocal or recurrent connections (A⇔B), and (4) intermediate stations, which bridge brain structures that are not directly connected

span.label: phenomenon: large-scale cortico-cortical network organisation
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: cortico-cortical connectivity of the mouse neocortex — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Examination of the full data set revealed that the neocortex is organized into several subnetworks that display unique topological organization, perhaps reflecting different information processing strategies for each.

span.label: builds-on → the double co-injection tract tracing method of Thompson and Swanson (2010)
span.quote: The MCP neuronal connectivity data was produced using double co-injection tract tracing ( Thompson and Swanson, 2010 ), which simultaneously reveals four types of information for a given region (i.e. A): its (1) inputs (A←B), (2) outputs (A→B), (3) reciprocal or recurrent connections (A⇔B), and (4) intermediate stations, which bridge brain structures that are not directly connected (A→C→B).

span.label: extends → cortical connectivity matrices previously assembled from literature data (Honey et al., 2007; Sporns et al., 2007; Markov et al., 2010)
span.quote: In contrast, the networks reported here are based on data collected and analyzed in a homogenous fashion rather than gathered piecemeal from the literature.

span.label: builds-on → the concept of cross-modal modulation (Driver and Noesselt, 2008; Stein and Stanford, 2008)
span.quote: This supports the concept of cross-modal modulation, which challenges the idea that mammalian primary sensory cortices are strictly unisensory ( Driver and Noesselt, 2008 ; Stein and Stanford, 2008 ).

span.label: extends → the account of the lateral entorhinal cortex as a gateway to the hippocampus (de Curtis and Paré, 2004)
span.quote: These data suggest that the ENTl is not only a gateway for neocortical information to the hippocampus ( de Curtis and Paré, 2004 ), but may also be a site of interaction for various cortical areas and between these neocortical areas and the amygdala, hippocampus, and olfactory cortical areas.

span.label: builds-on → the experimental procedures of Hintiryan et al. (2012)
span.quote: All experimental procedures have been described previously ( Hintiryan et al., 2012 ).

span.label: critiques → cortical connectivity matrices assembled piecemeal from the published literature
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS HOW THE DATA WERE ASSEMBLED. 'the networks reported here are based on data COLLECTED AND ANALYZED IN A HOMOGENOUS FASHION RATHER THAN GATHERED PIECEMEAL FROM THE LITERATURE.' A critique of provenance rather than of any result - and one this project should read against itself, since a cross-field corpus is assembled exactly the way this sentence criticises. Q-449.
span.quote: In contrast, the networks reported here are based on data collected and analyzed in a homogenous fashion rather than gathered piecemeal from the literature.

span.label: extends → human structural and functional network studies using fMRI and diffusion tensor imaging, which the paper holds need animal validation at higher resolution
span.quote: Nevertheless, it is necessary to validate these networks using reliable neural tract tracing methods in animal models at a higher resolution, which will facilitate exploration of the molecular and cellular etiologies of these disorders.

span.label: contradicts → the assumption that mammalian primary sensory cortices are strictly unisensory
span.quote: This supports the concept of cross-modal modulation, which challenges the idea that mammalian primary sensory cortices are strictly unisensory

span.label: builds-on → the network-science framing of brain organisation, including the hub concept
span.quote: The insular and temporal areas along the lateral aspect of the cortex formed two distinct clusters and the broad and unique intracortical connections of the claustrum and lateral entorhinal area suggest they may serve as hubs, or regions of high network interaction ( Sporns, 2010 ).

span.label: extends → wiring diagrams previously assembled only for specific functional systems or smaller scales
span.quote: Unlike the recently assembled connectome of the C. elegans ( White et al., 1986 ; Jarrell et al., 2012 ), wiring diagrams for mammalian species have been assembled on substantially smaller scales and for specific functional systems ( Felleman and Van Essen, 1991 ; Saleem et al., 2008 ).

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95

span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named neither tracer class. This sentence names both and pairs them as the two halves of every co-injection - the contrast is the design. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The MCP neuronal connectivity data was produced using double co-injection tract tracing ( Thompson and Swanson, 2010 ), which simultaneously reveals four types of information for a given region (i.e. A): its (1) inputs (A←B), (2) outputs (A→B), (3) reciprocal or recurrent connections (A⇔B), and (4) intermediate stations, which bridge brain structures that are not directly connected

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8
span.quote: The insular and temporal areas along the lateral aspect of the cortex formed two distinct clusters and the broad and unique intracortical connections of the claustrum and lateral entorhinal area suggest they may serve as hubs, or regions of high network interaction ( Sporns, 2010 ).

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8
span.quote: The matrices provide a condensed view of cortical connectivity patterns, but exclude details like projections routes, laminar specificity of projections, or topographical and topological connectivity patterns, which are critical features of networks.

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: The connectivity matrices and cortical map revealed that the entire cortex is organized into four somatic sensorimotor, two medial, and two lateral subnetworks that display unique topologies and can interact through select cortical areas.

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85
span.quote: the ENTl is also the starting point of the classic trisynaptic circuit that transfers information to the hippocampus

span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS Zingg2014-neural-networks-of-the-mouse-neocortex[2]: the relation was always stated, the endpoint names were not in the span.
span.quote: Each co-injection consists of one anterograde ( Phaseolus vulgaris leucoagglutinin, PHAL or biotinylated dextran amine, BDA) and one retrograde (cholera toxin subunit b, CTb or Fluorogold, FG) tracer.

span.label: cluster analysis
span.quote: To reveal subnetworks, a composite matrix was constructed in which the nodes (ROIs) were reordered via a clustering algorithm

span.label: percentage agreement between two methods
span.quote: Iterating through each matrix entry, 89% of connections exhibited mutual labeling by both anterograde and retrograde labeling methods, suggesting that the datasets were significantly similar.

span.label: weighted directional connectivity matrices
span.quote: To reveal subnetworks, a composite matrix was constructed in which the nodes (ROIs) were reordered via a clustering algorithm ( Figure 2E ; Supplemental Materials for annotation and analysis details).

span.label: clustering algorithm
span.quote: To reveal subnetworks, a composite matrix was constructed in which the nodes (ROIs) were reordered via a clustering algorithm ( Figure 2E ; Supplemental Materials for annotation and analysis details).

span.label: semi-quantitative densities
span.quote: The first is for the purpose of constructing a comprehensive connectivity database and is comprised of an excel sheet that indexes anatomic locations and corresponding semi-quantitative densities of labeling (PHAL labeled axons/terminal boutons; CTb and FG labeled neurons).

span.label: The mouse neocortex resolves into eight subnetworks: four somatic sensorimotor, two medial and two lateral, each with its own topology, communicating through selected cortical areas.
span.quote: The connectivity matrices and cortical map revealed that the entire cortex is organized into four somatic sensorimotor, two medial, and two lateral subnetworks that display unique topologies and can interact through select cortical areas.

span.label: Anterograde and retrograde tracing agreed on 89% of matrix entries, cross-validating the connectivity dataset.
span.quote: Iterating through each matrix entry, 89% of connections exhibited mutual labeling by both anterograde and retrograde labeling methods, suggesting that the datasets were significantly similar.

span.label: The claustrum's cortical connectivity is asymmetric: it receives bilateral cortical input but sends output almost exclusively to the same hemisphere.
span.quote: The intracortical connectivity of the CLA displays a unique asymmetric pattern: cortical inputs to the CLA are bilateral, but outputs from CLA are almost exclusively ipsilateral

span.label: The temporal association, ectorhinal and perirhinal areas are back-labelled from layers 2 and 5a of the entire neocortex except ACAv, RSP and VISp, meaning this subnetwork collects input from nearly the whole cortex.
span.quote: A retrograde tracer injection in all three structures back labeled neurons in layers 2 and 5a of the entire neocortex with the exception of the ACAv, RSP, and VISp

span.label: Because every main node of the four somatic sensorimotor subnetworks is reciprocally connected, sensory and motor areas can interact directly without routing through higher-order association cortex.
span.quote: This organization allows direct interactions between sensory and motor areas in the absence of higher order association areas.

span.label: The medial subnetwork contains direct reciprocal connections between visual, auditory and primary somatosensory areas, which argues against mammalian primary sensory cortices being strictly unisensory.
span.quote: This supports the concept of cross-modal modulation, which challenges the idea that mammalian primary sensory cortices are strictly unisensory

span.label: The second medial subnetwork is a serial chain running from dorsal subiculum to RSPv to ACAv and then to the infralimbic, prelimbic and medial orbitofrontal areas.
span.quote: The second medial subnetwork is topologically distinct from the first in that it successively transmits information from the SUBd to the RSPv to the ACAv and then to the ILA, PL, and ORBm.

span.label: Ventral retrosplenial cortex is the sole neocortical area receiving dense dorsal subicular input, making it the entry point for dorsal hippocampal information into neocortex.
span.quote: The RSPv is the only neocortical recipient of dense inputs from the SUBd, through which information processed in the dorsal hippocampus can reach the neocortex

span.label: The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is where all four somatic sensorimotor subnetworks converge.
span.quote: The PFCdl receives a confluence of information from all four somatic sensorimotor subnetworks.

span.label: The ventromedial prefrontal cortex is where the medial and lateral subnetworks converge, letting external sensory and internal visceral/gustatory information be integrated.
span.quote: The PFCvm receives convergent inputs from the medial and lateral subnetworks and provides an interface for integrating or communicating information regarding external stimuli (such as visual, auditory, somatic sensory) and internal stimuli (such as visceral and gustatory information).

span.label: 89% of connections were labelled by both the anterograde and retrograde methods, so the two datasets largely agree
span.quote: Iterating through each matrix entry, 89% of connections exhibited mutual labeling by both anterograde and retrograde labeling methods, suggesting that the datasets were significantly similar.

span.label: clustering placed every node into a small number of distinct cortico-cortical modules
span.quote: The clustering demonstrated that all nodes fall into a few relatively distinct cortico-cortical subnetwork modules

span.label: the four somatic sensorimotor modules each formed a separate subnetwork
span.quote: Each of the four somatic sensorimotor modules ( orofaciopharyngeal, upper limb, lower limb/trunk, and whisker ) formed distinct subnetworks.

span.label: the claustrum and lateral entorhinal area have broad unique connections consistent with a hub role
span.quote: The insular and temporal areas along the lateral aspect of the cortex formed two distinct clusters and the broad and unique intracortical connections of the claustrum and lateral entorhinal area suggest they may serve as hubs, or regions of high network interaction ( Sporns, 2010 ).

span.label: claustral connectivity is asymmetric: inputs bilateral, outputs almost exclusively ipsilateral
span.quote: The intracortical connectivity of the CLA displays a unique asymmetric pattern: cortical inputs to the CLA are bilateral, but outputs from CLA are almost exclusively ipsilateral

span.label: the temporal subnetwork receives input from and projects back to nearly the entire neocortex
span.quote: A retrograde tracer injection in all three structures back labeled neurons in layers 2 and 5a of the entire neocortex with the exception of the ACAv, RSP, and VISp ( Figure 5C-D ) suggesting that this subnetwork receives input from nearly the entire neocortex.

span.label: within the somatic sensorimotor subnetworks, sensory and motor areas interact directly without higher-order association areas
span.quote: Within the somatic sensorimotor network, all main somatic nodes within the four subnetworks are heavily and reciprocally connected. This organization allows direct interactions between sensory and motor areas in the absence of higher order association areas.

span.label: the lateral subnetworks are points of massive convergence, each connected to a large number of cortical areas
span.quote: The lateral subnetworks represent a point of massive convergence in the cortex. Interactions are centered on two major components: the AI in the anterolateral insula subnetwork, and the TEa/PERI/ECT complex in the posterolateral temporal subnetwork. Each receives input from, and projects back to, an extensive number of cortical areas.

span.label: each subnetwork converges onto a discrete territory of prefrontal cortex
span.quote: Projections from each of the identified subnetworks topographically converge onto discrete regions of the prefrontal cortex.

span.label: neighbouring prefrontal zones are largely segregated from one another despite adjacency
span.quote: The relative segregation of these prefrontal zones combined with their specific cortical inputs and subcortical targets may help define their unique processing role and contribution to behavior.

span.label: about 600 pathways from around 317 co-injections are available, 304 efferent and 296 afferent
span.quote: Currently, a total of ~600 pathways (304 efferent and 296 afferent) associated with ~317 co-injections are available ( Figure S3 for injections; Table S1 for list of selected cases, Table S2 for abbreviations).

span.label: direct reciprocal connections among visual, auditory and somatosensory areas support cross-modal modulation
span.quote: This supports the concept of cross-modal modulation, which challenges the idea that mammalian primary sensory cortices are strictly unisensory

span.label: macro- or meso-connectome
span.quote: constructing a brain-wide connectivity diagram for all well-defined gray matter regions, i.e., the macro- or meso-connectome

span.label: hub
span.quote: suggest they may serve as hubs, or regions of high network interaction

span.quote: Each co-injection consists of one anterograde ( Phaseolus vulgaris leucoagglutinin, PHAL or biotinylated dextran amine, BDA) and one retrograde (cholera toxin subunit b, CTb or Fluorogold, FG) tracer.

span.label: iConnectome
span.quote: The iConnectom e is an online resource that presents high-resolution whole-brain images of neural connectivity in several different formats.

span.term: intraconnectivity versus interconnectivity read off the matrix diagonal
span.quote: The number of connections within these groupings near the diagonal reflects the density of intraconnectivity within a subnetwork, while connections farther from the diagonal demonstrate a subnetwork’s interconnectivity with other subnetworks.

span.label: meso-connectome
span.quote: Numerous studies have examined the neuronal inputs and/or outputs of many areas of the brain cortex, but how these areas organize into broader communication networks across the cortex is unclear.

span.label: double co-injection

span.label: clustering
span.quote: The clustering orders nodes into modules that maximize the connectivity and arrange highly interconnected nodes such that they are clustered along the matrix diagonal, facilitating visualization of grouped regions that can be considered subnetworks.

span.label: location of the tracer co-injection site
span.term: location of the tracer co-injection site
span.quote: In one animal, two confined, non-overlapping co-injections are placed into different brain regions

span.label: distribution and semi-quantitative density of anterograde and retrograde labelling
span.term: distribution and semi-quantitative density of anterograde and retrograde labelling
span.quote: To begin building cortical networks, data within all regions was annotated by manually recording the distribution of anterograde and retrograde labeling.

span.label: animal age, sex and strain held constant (8 week old male C57Bl/6J)
span.term: animal age, sex and strain held constant (8 week old male C57Bl/6J)
span.quote: In brief, double co-injections of tracers were made into different areas of the entire neocortex, hippocampus, olfactory cortical areas, and amygdala of 8 week old male C57Bl/6J mice.

span.label: tracer transport time held constant at one week
span.term: tracer transport time held constant at one week
span.quote: One week was allowed for tracer transport after which animals were perfused and their brains extracted.

span.label: density of intraconnectivity
span.quote: The clustering orders nodes into modules that maximize the connectivity and arrange highly interconnected nodes such that they are clustered along the matrix diagonal, facilitating visualization of grouped regions that can be considered subnetworks. The number of connections within these groupings near the diagonal reflects the density of intraconnectivity within a subnetwork

span.label: laminar distribution patterns
span.quote: The matrices provide a condensed view of cortical connectivity patterns, but exclude details like projections routes, laminar specificity of projections, or topographical and topological connectivity patterns, which are critical features of networks.

span.label: anterograde and retrograde labeling
span.quote: Iterating through each matrix entry, 89% of connections exhibited mutual labeling by both anterograde and retrograde labeling methods, suggesting that the datasets were significantly similar.

span.label: Over 600 — labelled neuronal pathways collected across the whole mouse neocortex
span.quote: Over 600 labeled neuronal pathways acquired from tracer injections placed across the entire mouse neocortex enabled us to generate a cortical connectivity atlas.

span.label: 240 — intracortical connections manually reconstructed into the common atlas frame
span.quote: 240 intracortical connections were manually reconstructed within a common neuroanatomic framework, forming a cortico-cortical connectivity map that facilitates comparison of connections from different cortical targets.

span.label: 89% — share of matrix entries labelled by both the anterograde and the retrograde method
span.quote: Iterating through each matrix entry, 89% of connections exhibited mutual labeling by both anterograde and retrograde labeling methods, suggesting that the datasets were significantly similar.

span.label: ~600 pathways (304 efferent and 296 afferent), ~317 co-injections — contents of the released dataset at time of publication
span.quote: Currently, a total of ~600 pathways (304 efferent and 296 afferent) associated with ~317 co-injections are available

span.label: 80 anterograde and 160 retrograde — pathways included in the reconstructed cortico-cortical connectivity map
span.quote: This map includes 80 anterograde (PHAL) and 160 retrograde pathways (CTb and FG).

span.label: ~ 250-500μm — diameter of the tracer co-injection sites
span.quote: The size of co-injections are ~ 250-500μm and mostly confined within individual cortical areas

span.label: 50μm — section thickness used for all brains
span.quote: All brains were sliced at 50μm thickness using a Compresstome

span.label: over 600 labeled neuronal pathways — the atlas contents
span.quote: Over 600 labeled neuronal pathways acquired from tracer injections placed across the entire mouse neocortex enabled us to generate a cortical connectivity atlas.

span.label: 240 — intracortical connections manually reconstructed into the common frame
span.quote: 240 intracortical connections were manually reconstructed within a common neuroanatomic framework, forming a cortico-cortical connectivity map that facilitates comparison of connections from different cortical targets.

span.label: 89% — connections labelled by both tracer directions
span.quote: Iterating through each matrix entry, 89% of connections exhibited mutual labeling by both anterograde and retrograde labeling methods, suggesting that the datasets were significantly similar.

span.label: ~250-500μm — co-injection size, mostly confined within individual cortical areas
span.quote: The size of co-injections are ~ 250-500μm and mostly confined within individual cortical areas ( Figure 1B ), although when images are adjusted to reveal fine fibers, injection sites are overexposed, misrepresenting their actual size ( Figure S1A ).

span.label: 304 efferent and 296 afferent — pathway counts from about 317 co-injections
span.quote: Currently, a total of ~600 pathways (304 efferent and 296 afferent) associated with ~317 co-injections are available ( Figure S3 for injections; Table S1 for list of selected cases, Table S2 for abbreviations).

span.label: 8 week old male C57Bl/6J mice — the animals
span.quote: In brief, double co-injections of tracers were made into different areas of the entire neocortex, hippocampus, olfactory cortical areas, and amygdala of 8 week old male C57Bl/6J mice.
